paragraphs.text: Meaning “Jehovah Loosens [the womb]”; or, “Jehovah Exalts.” Heb., Yir·meyaʹhu.
Meaning “My Portion Is Jehovah.” Heb., Chil·qi·yaʹhu.
“Of Zedekiah.” Heb., leTsidh·qi·yaʹhu, meaning “Jehovah Is Righteousness.”
“An almond tree.” Heb., sha·qedhʹ, “awakening one”; one of the first trees to bloom in the spring.
“Am keeping awake.” Heb., sho·qedhʹ, corresponding to sha·qedhʹ in vs 11.
“Blown upon,” as respects the fire underneath. Or, “set aflame,” suggesting a furnace.
“And toward the people of the land.” Heb., u·leʽamʹ ha·ʼaʹrets. Later used contemptuously. Compare Joh 7:47-49.
Lit., “Let there be a going.” In Heb. this is a verb in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.
“My,” in the original Heb. text; MLXXSyVg, “its.” One of the Eighteen Emendations of the Sopherim made out of a misapplied reverence for Jehovah God. See App 2B.
“In very great horror,” by a correction; M, “be [pl.] very much devastated.”
Or, “Is Israel a slave.” Heb., ha·ʽeʹvedh Yis·ra·ʼelʹ.
“Your gods.” Heb., ʼelo·heyʹkha, pl. of ʼelohʹah, with eyʹkha, “your,” masc. sing., addressed to “Judah.”
“You,” fem. sing., addressed to Jerusalem, or Zion.
“Blood marks.” LXX, “bloods.” Lit., “blood,” sing. in M, but the accompanying Heb. verb for “have been found” and the following Heb. pronoun for “them” are pl.
“The souls of.” Heb., naph·shohthʹ; Gr., psy·khonʹ; Lat., a·ni·maʹrum. See App 4A.
“You,” fem. sing., addressed to Jerusalem, or Zion.
Lit., “the unfaithfulness (apostasy), Israel,” thus terming Israel a concrete example of unfaithfulness, or apostasy.
Or, “your state of unfaithfulness.” Lit., “your unfaithfulnesses.”
“To the men of.” Heb., leʼishʹ, sing. but used collectively.
“Men of.” Heb., ʼish, sing. but used collectively.
Lit., “Call out, be full [do it fully].”
“The soul.” Heb., han·naʹphesh; Gr., psy·khesʹ; Lat., aʹni·mam. See App 4A.
“There will be a rendering.” In Heb. this is a verb in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.
“Your way and your dealings have done these things to you,” in agreement with TLXXSyVg and some Heb. mss.
Or, “but an extermination I shall not carry out.”
“And into the rocks.” Heb., u·vak·ke·phimʹ; Gr., peʹtras. Compare Mt 16:18 ftn, “Rock-mass.”
“You,” fem. sing., addressed to Zion, or Jerusalem.
“A woman having childbirth pains,” by a slight correction.
Or, “by what are no gods.” Heb., beloʼʹ ʼelo·himʹ.
“Her terrace walls,” by a slight change of vowel pointing.
Or, “foreign gods.” Lit., “a god [or, gods] of a foreign (country).” Heb., ʼelo·hehʹ ne·kharʹ. The pl. form of “god” may denote excellence.
“A ruinous [trap].” Or, “ruination,” that is, in the form of a trap or snare.
“Which,” referring to the “very word,” both masc. sing.
Or, “saying, ‘Perfect peace!’ ” Lit., “saying, ‘Peace! Peace!’ ” See Isa 26:3 ftn, “Peace.”
“Do not go out,” fem., addressed to the “daughter” of Zion in vs 23.
“One making a thorough search” (like a grape gatherer), by a change of vowel pointing; M, “as a fortified place.”
Lit., “the sullen ones of the stubborn ones.”
“Have been scorched,” by one derivation of the Heb. verb; by another derivation, “have snorted.”
“Temple of.” Heb., heh·khalʹ; Gr., na·osʹ; Lat., temʹplum. Compare 2Ki 20:18 ftn. See Mt 23:16 ftn.
“To the ‘queen of.’ ” Heb., lim·leʹkheth; LXX, “to the army”; 52 Heb. mss, “to the work (worship) of.”
“There is a pouring out.” In Heb. this is a verb in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.
“Your,” fem. sing., addressed to Zion, or Jerusalem.
“In the valley of the son of Hinnom.” Heb., beghehʼʹ ven-Hin·nomʹ; Gr., en phaʹrag·gi hui·ouʹ En·nomʹ; Lat., in valʹle fiʹli·i Enʹnom. See App 4C.
Or, “because of there being no place [else].”
“[When] I shall [or, would] without fail gather them,” by a change of vowel pointing.
Or, “put us out of action,” that is, caused us to perish.
MLXX end chapter 8 here with this as vs 23.
“A slaughtering arrow,” M; Mmargin, “a hammered arrow”; by another derivation, “an arrow from a special wood [bow].”
Or, “for our residences have been thrown away,” in agreement with Vg.
Or, “in [his] foreskin,” a sign of uncircumcision. Or, “among the uncircumcision [the ones who are uncircumcised, having foreskins].”
“Is in truth God.” Heb., ʼElo·himʹ ʼemethʹ.
“The gods.” Aram., ʼela·hai·yaʼʹ. This entire vs is written in Aram.
“Productive land.” Heb., te·velʹ; LXX, “inhabited earth”; Lat., orʹbem, “circle,” that is, of the earth.
“Sluices,” by reading beda·qimʹ instead of bera·qimʹ, “lightnings”; MTLXXSyVg, “lightnings.” See JTS, Vol. 3, 1952, pp. 214-216. Compare Ps 135:7 ftn, “Sluices.”
“Wind.” Heb., ruʹach; Lat., venʹtum; Gr., phos, “light.”
Or, “breath.” Heb., ruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma; Lat., spiʹri·tus.
Or, “who have not come to know you.”
“Men of.” Heb., ʼish, sing. but used collectively.
“In regard to their calamity,” M; TLXXSyVg and 34 Heb. mss, “in the time of their calamity.”
“Seeking for your soul,” MSyVg; LXX, “seeking for my soul”; T, “seeking to put you to death.”
Or, “you are confident (trusting).” LXXא,B, “you are not confident.”
“From your heads,” by a correction in agreement with LXXSyVg.
“Your,” sing., by a correction in agreement with LXX; MSyVg, “your,” pl.
Or, “small; young,” such as attendants, servants.
In Heb. this is a verb in the infinitive absolute.
“Full amount.” Or, “double amount; duplicate.” Heb., mish·nehʹ.
“From the ends (terminations) of the earth.” Heb., me·ʼaph·seh-ʼaʹrets. Compare 25:31.
“Their,” ThSyVg and about 170 Heb. mss; M, “your,” pl.
“For your souls.” Heb., benaph·shoh·theh·khemʹ, pl. of neʹphesh; Gr., psy·khasʹ; Lat., aʹni·mas. See App 4A.
“Men of.” Heb., ʼish, sing. but in a collective sense.
Or, “Do not make atonement for.” Heb., ʼal-tekhap·perʹ.
“Valley of the son of Hinnom.” Heb., gehʼ ven-Hin·nomʹ; Lat., valʹlem fiʹli·i Enʹnom. See App 4C.

“Gate of the Potsherds.” Because this gate opened upon the most easterly section of the valley of Hinnom, it is likely identical with the Gate of the Ash-heaps, or the Dung Gate. In Jerusalem in the Old Testament, p. 230, ftn 1, Dr. J. Simons says: “Instead of ‘Gate of the Potsherds’ it is possible to translate ‘Gate of the Potters’, or, better perhaps, ‘Gate of the Earthenware Pots.’ ”
Lit., “because of there being no place.”
“Pashhur.” According to the Judeo-Aramaic derivation this name means “What Remains Round About” (Heb., pash, “it remains” and sechohrʹ, “round about”).
“Fright all around.” Or, “Magormissabib.” Heb., Ma·ghohrʹ mis·sa·vivʹ.
“To endure it,” in agreement with LXXVg.
“Fright all around.” Heb., ma·ghohrʹ mis·sa·vivʹ. Compare vs 3 ftn, “Around.”
Lit., “mortal man [Heb., ʼenohshʹ] of my peace.”
“Your,” fem. sing., referring to the city.
“Coniah,” M(Heb., Kon·yaʹhu)T; LXXSyVg, “Jeconiah”; in 2Ki 24:6-15, “Jehoiachin.” The grandson of Josiah.
“Their soul (soulful desire).” Heb., naph·shamʹ; Gr., psy·khaisʹ au·tonʹ; Lat., aʹni·mam suʹam.
“Jehovah Is Our Righteousness.” Heb., Yehwahʹ Tsidh·qeʹnu.
“And like an able-bodied man.” Heb., u·khegheʹver.
“God.” Heb., ha·ʼElo·hehʹ. Here ha is an interrogative particle introducing a question.
“And say, ‘Jehovah says,’ ” Vg; Sy, “and are saying, ‘Jehovah himself has said thus.’ ”
Or, “What is the pronouncement?” Heb., mah-mas·saʼʹ.

For the rendering “You people are—⁠O what a burden!” see VT, Vol. VI, 1956, pp. 315, 316. Heb., ʼeth-mah-mas·saʼʹ! Thus in answer to the people’s question mah-mas·saʼʹ? Jeremiah puns and replies, ʼeth-mah-mas·saʼʹ! LXXVgc(Lat., vos eʹstis oʹnus), “You people are the burden.”
“The living God.” Heb., ʼElo·himʹ chai·yimʹ, both pl.
“Jeconiah.” Heb., Yekhon·yaʹhu, meaning “Jehovah Firmly Establishes”; abbreviated to “Coniah” in 22:24, 28 and 37:1; same as “Jehoiachin” in 2Ki 24:8.

“Sheshach,” MVg; T, “Babel.” This appears to be a cryptographic name for Babel (Babylon) by the device called ʼath·bashʹ that disguises the true name by taking the last letter of the Heb. alphabet, Taw, for the first, ʼAʹleph, and the second to the last letter, Shin, for the second letter, Behth, and so on. Thus in “Babel” each Behth, “b,” would stand for Shin, Laʹmedh would stand for Kaph, and the name would become She·shakhʹ.
Or, “most distant part; extremity.” Heb., qetsehʹ. Compare 16:19. See Ac 1:8.
Or, “from the farthest part of the earth to the farthermost part of the earth.” Heb., miq·tsehʹ ha·ʼaʹrets weʽadh-qetsehʹ ha·ʼaʹrets. Compare vs 31.
Or, “your days for being slaughtered and for your being scattered have come due.”
“Sword,” TLXX and about 20 Heb. mss; M, “heatedness (burning).”
Lit., “men.” Heb., ʼana·shimʹ, pl. of ʼish.
“Micah,” Mmargin and a number of Heb. mss; M, “Micaiah.”
Meaning “My Light Is Jehovah.” Heb., ʼU·ri·yaʹhu; found only here and in vss 21, 23.
“Jehoiakim,” MTLXXVg; Sy, the Arabic version and three Heb. mss, “Zedekiah,” as in vss 3, 12.
“Their masters.” Heb., ʼadho·neh·khemʹ, pl. of ʼa·dhohnʹ, to denote more than one.
“Nebuchadnezzar,” in 27:6–29:3; in 21:2 and elsewhere throughout the book, “Nebuchadrezzar.”
“The grand overseer.” Lit., “overseers.” Heb., peqi·dhimʹ, pl. to denote grandeur.
“It,” fem. sing., apparently referring to the “exile” in vss 14, 16.
“Your,” fem. sing., referring to the city of Zion.
Lit., “there was a walking.” In Heb. this is a verb in the infinitive absolute, indefinite as to time and impersonal.
“You,” fem. sing., referring to the “virgin” in vs 4.
Or, “the way that you have gone.”
“Had husbandly ownership of them,” MVg; T, “was finding pleasure for myself in them”; LXX, “had no concern for them”; Sy, “despised them.”
“The statutes of,” MTSyVg; LXX and one Heb. ms omit.

“Coming,” MmarginTLXXSyVg and 48 Heb. mss. In M the Heb. consonants for this participle are missing, but the vowel points have been inserted to indicate “coming” is to be read. This is qere but not kethib (read but not written).
A shekel weighed 11.4 g (0.367 oz t).
“The mighty One.” Heb., hag·Gib·bohrʹ. Compare Isa 9:6 and Isa 10:21 ftns, “God.”
“The sons of men.” Heb., benehʹ ʼa·dhamʹ.
Or, “and among other men.” Heb., u·va·ʼa·dhamʹ.
“And the men of.” Heb., weʼishʹ, sing. but in a collective sense.
Lit., “the field,” sing. but in a collective sense.
Lit., “a man sitting.” Heb., ʼish yo·shevʹ.
Or, “where they wish.” Lit., “free to their soul.” Compare De 21:14 ftn.
“The men.” Heb., ha·ʼana·shimʹ, pl. of ʼish.
Lit., “they cut.” Heb., kor·thuʹ; the same as for cutting the calf.
“The people of the land.” Heb., ʽam ha·ʼaʹrets.
“A man of the [true] God.” Heb., ʼish ha·ʼElo·himʹ. See App 1F.
“Jehonadab.” Heb., Yehoh·na·dhavʹ, as in 2Ki 10:15, where see ftn.
“To the men of.” Heb., leʼishʹ, sing. but used collectively.
Meaning “Who Is Like Jehovah?” Heb., Mi·khaiʹhu.
“And Delaiah.” Heb., u·Dhela·yaʹhu, meaning “Jehovah Has Drawn Up [in deliverance].”
Meaning “Jehovah Has Shown Favor; Jehovah Has Been Gracious.” Heb., Chanan·yaʹhu.
Meaning “Jehovah Is Recompense”; or, “Communion Sacrifice of Jehovah.” Heb., She·lem·yaʹhu.
Meaning “My Lamp Is Jehovah.” Heb., Ne·ri·yaʹhu.
“The ninth month,” that is, Chislev, the postexilic name of the ninth Jewish lunar month that corresponds to the latter half of November and the first half of December. See App 8B.
Meaning “Jehovah Has Concealed [or, Treasured].” Heb., Tsephan·yaʹhu.
“And Gedaliah.” Heb., u·Ghedhal·yaʹhu, meaning “Great Is Jehovah.”
Meaning “My King Is Jehovah.” Heb., Mal·ki·yaʹhu.
“This city will be burned,” TLXXSy; M, “this city you will burn.”
Or, “the chief court official; the chief attendant.” Heb., Rav-sa·risʹ.
Or, “the chief magician (soothsayer; astrologer); the chief of the great ones.” Heb., Rav-maghʹ.
“And Jezaniah.” Heb., wI·zan·yaʹhu, meaning “Jehovah Gives Ear.”
“Should he strike you to the soul,” that is, mortally. Heb., yak·kekʹkah neʹphesh; Gr., pa·taʹxei sou psy·khenʹ; Lat., in·ter·fiʹci·at aʹni·mam tuʹam. See App 4A.
“Was a great cistern,” LXX; M, “by the hand (at the instance) of Gedaliah.”
“Against your souls.” Heb., benaph·shoh·theh·khemʹ; Gr., psy·khaisʹ; Lat., aʹni·mas. See App 4A.
Lit., “House of the Sun.” Heb., Behth Sheʹmesh; Lat., doʹmus soʹlis; Gr., He·liʹou poʹle·os, “City of the Sun.”
“To the work (worship) of the heavens,” about 30 Heb. mss. Compare 7:18 ftn, “Queen.”
Lit., “there will be a pouring.” In Heb. this is a verb in the infinitive absolute.
“Also, when,” M; Sy, “And all the women answered and said, ‘When.’ ”
“And the people of the land.” Heb., weʽamʹ ha·ʼaʹrets.
“Cush,” M; TSy, “Cushite men”; LXX, “warriors of the Ethiopians”; Vg, “Ethiopia.”
Or, “Amen.” M, ʼA·mohnʹ, an Egyptian word.
“From No,” M; TVg, “of Alexandria”; LXX, “her son”; Sy, “of the waters.” Also known as Thebes.
“Their soul.” Heb., naph·shamʹ; Lat., aʹni·mam. See App 4A.
Lit., “your soul,” sing. but in a collective sense. Heb., naph·shekhemʹ; Gr., psy·khasʹ; Lat., aʹni·mas.
“A juniper tree.” The meaning of the Heb. word is uncertain; by a correction in agreement with LXX, “a wild ass.”
“Their,” masc. pl., referring to the men of Moab.
Or, “to his gods.” Heb., leʼ·lo·havʹ; Lat., diʹis.
“Malcam” (meaning “Their King”), M; LXXSyVg, “Melchom”; LXXא,B, “Melchol”; T, “their king.”
“Gad,” MLXXSyVg; T, “the land of Gad”; LXXא,A,B, “Gilead.”
“Those having understanding,” in agreement with LXXSy; MTVg, “the sons.”
Or, “son of earthling man.” Heb., ben-ʼa·dhamʹ.
“You,” MmarginTLXXVg and more than 100 Heb. mss; MSy, “them.”
“Of Elam,” MmarginTLXXSyVg and many Heb. mss; M, “to (of) time indefinite.”
“Chaldea,” LXXVg; TSy, “the land of the Chaldeans”; M, “the Chaldeans,” but with a fem. sing. verb.
“Their Repurchaser (Redeemer).” By extension of thought, “Their Avenger (Vindicator).” Heb., go·ʼalamʹ; Lat., re·demʹptor e·oʹrum. See Job 19:25 and Ps 19:14 ftns.
Lit., “daughters of an ostrich.” Compare Le 11:16 ftn, “Ostrich.”
Or, “the son of men.” Heb., ben-ʼa·dhamʹ.

“Leb-kamai.” Heb., Lev qa·maiʹ, meaning “The Heart of Those Rising Up Against Me.” This appears to be a cryptographic name for Chaldea (Kas·dimʹ), by the device called ʼath·bashʹ. T, “the land of the Chaldeans”; LXX, “the Chaldeans.” See 25:26 ftn.
“By his own soul.” Heb., benaph·shohʹ; Lat., per aʹni·mam suʹam; LXX, “by his arm.” See App 4A.
Or, “creeping, unwinged locusts.” See Joe 1:4 ftn.
“Productive land.” Heb., te·velʹ; LXX, “inhabited earth”; Lat., orʹbem, “circle,” that is, of the earth.
“Wind.” Heb., ruʹach; Lat., venʹtum; Gr., phos, “light.”
Or, “breath.” Heb., ruʹach; Gr., pneuʹma; Lat., spiʹri·tus.
“Chaldea,” Vg; T, “land of the Chaldeans”; MLXXSy, “Chaldeans.”
“Bristly locusts.” Or, “bristly, creeping, unwinged locusts.” See Joe 1:4 ftn.
“Papyrus boats,” by a slight correction; M, “swamp reeds; reedy pools.”
“Swoon away,” by a correction; T, “not be strong”; LXX, “be stupefied (stunned)”; Vg, “slumber.”
“They may die the second death,” T.
“And they will die the second death,” T.
“With,” MSyVg; T, “in the legation of”; LXX, “from.”
Lit., “prince of the resting-place.” Heb., sar menu·chahʹ.
“For the people of the land.” Heb., leʽamʹ ha·ʼaʹrets.
“Under [the sea], the carriages,” MTVg; LXX, “under the sea”; Sy, “under the sides of the sea.”
Lit., “from those seeing the king’s face.”
“The people of the land.” Heb., ʽam ha·ʼaʹrets.
LXX and 2Ki 25 omit the contents of vss 28-30.
Lit., “a thing of a day on its day.”
